texts: good. the thin fog, its coming in off the sea (the phrasal verb kept whole, the fog as the thing moved, the sea as source), the evening slot and the Year 1 date are all carried. The one caveat you cannot write around: 'day 246 of Year 1' goes into the calendar day-of-month slot as (Day 246), because the translator has no day-of-year term.

good. the fog is the agent of the reducing, visibility the object, and the Cliff Path is typed as a named path and recorded as the location of the reducing (not as a restriction on the visibility, which is the ordinary reading of the phrase).

mixed: the keep/result/continuation shape is right, but 'burning' is an activity rather than an adjectival state, so the shape's mandatory flat half comes out as (Member <lantern> burn) - the lantern itself typed as a burning event, which is ill-formed and matches nothing useful. Rewrite with an adjectival result and the burning as its own finite clause: 'Coraline Ash kept the lantern of the Harbor Station lit, and the lantern burned steadily.'
good. producing creates the mist-light, so it is the patient, the compound gets its mist_light to light genus, and the same mist-light symbol carries into the next two sentences.
good. show puts the mist-light in the theme slot (it is displayed, not changed) and 'at night' in the time slot.
good. the bare plural becomes a group witness with a nightmoth to moth genus, and the mist-light is the attractor.
good. the landing is emitted both as a group event and as a fireable per-member rule over the group, so a moth named later gets its own landing.

bad: two things go wrong - the threads sit in the patient slot, which asserts the moths changed them when they only deposited them, and the per-member rule hands every individual moth the whole shared thread group, i.e. claims each moth left all the threads. If the deposit is collective, say so and the per-member over-claim disappears: 'Together, the nightmoths left silken threads on the lantern.' (If you do mean a batch per moth, write 'Each nightmoth left its own silken threads on the lantern.') The patient-versus-theme slotting is a translator-side fix, not something your wording controls.

bad: 'about thirty-five' has no licensed carrier - the count slot takes a plain integer, so the hedge was improvised as a statistical distribution that no counting query will match - and because the phrase is indefinite, the collected threads form a fresh group with no link to the threads the moths left on the lantern. Rewrite with an explicit bound and a partitive: 'Coraline Ash collected at least thirty and at most forty of the silken threads from the lantern the next morning.' If the round figure matters more than the hedge, 'thirty-five of the silken threads' parses exactly.
